To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fetal liver cells obtained after circulation arrest of fetuses kept in a refrigerator at 4 C for 16 hours are still viable for transplantation, and that the test for the viability using trypan blue gives results reflecting better the number of haemopoetic stem cells (CFUs-S) than the number of committed cells (GM-CFU).
fetal liver cells kept in refrigerator at +4 degrees C for 16 hours after circulatory arrest contain a significant proportion of viable haemopoietetic stem cells and committed progenitor cells.

the use of fetal liver cells as a source of transplants for haematopoietic reconstitution is limited by the time needed to transport the material from the laboratory to the place of its use, and the duration of storage of the material in refrigerator at 5 degrees C.

the best test for the assessment of viability of haemopoeitc fetal liver cells is the one using the trypan blue method, which allows the assessment of the number of CFUs-S, but the use of the GM-CFU test is not excluded.

the best test for assessment of the viability and usefulness of the haemopoesis stem cells obtained from the liver of mouse fetuses kept in refrigeration at 4 degrees Celsius is the clonial test for GM-CFU cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in order to evaluate the number of haemopoiesic stem cells in a given organ, the test with tryphan blue is the best choice.
the test with tryphan blue is more sensitive than the test with CFU-S in detecting hypoxia of fetal liver.

the test based on the splenic colony formation of CFU-S is a good method for the evaluation of the number of haemopoiesic stem cells in the liver of the mouse fetus kept in a refrigerator at 4 degree C for 16 hours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the test for the viability based on clonal GM-CFU growth in agar is not a good predictor of the number of haemopoiesic stem cells.
fetal liver cells kept in refrigerator for a short time are still able to support haemopoietis reconstitution.
the cells from fetal liver kept at 4 degrees can be still used for transplantation of haemopoiesic cells.
